title: Moiré-enabled chiral plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands
authors: Magnus Husted, Viktor Kanstrup, Eduardo J. C. Dias, Joel D. Cox
abstract: Twisting two stacked graphene layers superimposes a moiré superlattice that reshapes their electronic structure, yet how it shapes the collective optical response of finite, nanoscale bilayers remains largely unexplored. Using an atomistic tight-binding and self-consistent density-matrix approach, we compute the twist-dependent plasmonic response of twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands comprising thousands of atoms. The spectra are strongly tunable and split into two regimes at a critical angle where a single moiré wavelength spans the island; beyond it, an ordered ladder of resonances emerges whenever an integer number of moiré periods fits within the overlapping bilayer. In doped islands, the interlayer coupling also produces a moiré-enabled Born--Kuhn chiral plasmon: opposite transverse dipoles in the two layers form an electric quadrupole that hybridizes with the bright dipole, opening an anticrossing near the critical angle, with a handedness that reverses with the twist direction. Triangular islands confirm that the moiré lattice, not the flake boundary, governs both effects, establishing twist as a mechanical handle on chiral graphene plasmons.
summary: This theoretical work models the optical properties of twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands, showing that the moiré superlattice fundamentally controls the electronic response. Key findings include the formation of resonance ladders and the emergence of a moiré-enabled chiral plasmon, demonstrating that twist angle acts as a powerful tuning knob for these quantum optical phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates how the moiré superlattice formed by twisting two stacked graphene layers modifies the collective optical response of finite, nanoscale bilayers.
main_result: The moiré lattice dictates the emergence of an ordered resonance ladder and enables a moiré-enabled Born-Kuhn chiral plasmon, confirming twist as a mechanical handle for graphene plasmons.
method: The authors employed an atomistic tight-binding and self-consistent density-matrix approach to compute the twist-dependent plasmonic response.
model_or_system: The physical system is twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) nanoislands (hexagonal and triangular geometries). The model incorporates edge effects and the moiré superlattice periodicity, analyzing the optical response ($\sigma_{ext}$) as a function of twist angle ($	heta$) and doping ($\eta$).
key_observables: Extinction cross section ($\sigma_{ext}$), Born-Kuhn pseudoscalar ($C(\omega)$), and the emergence of resonance ladders.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), moiré wavelength ($\lambda_m$), doping level ($\eta$), and the critical angle ($	heta_m$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the quasistatic approximation and operates in the linear-response regime for optical calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of $\sigma_{ext}$ on $	heta$ for both undoped and doped cases, showing the resonance ladder and the anticrossing associated with the chiral plasmon near $	heta_m$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the optical response by first establishing the role of the moiré lattice in creating resonance ladders, then focusing on the doped regime to derive the chiral plasmon signature via interlayer coupling, and finally confirming these effects using different island geometries.
why_interesting: The explicit calculation of chiral plasmons and the use of the Born-Kuhn pseudoscalar to quantify handedness provides a rich theoretical framework applicable to understanding topological and symmetry-protected excitations in low-dimensional quantum materials.
